$schema: MIGRAPILOT_STATUS — canonical cross-agent state. Update on every material change.

rules.easyFirst: Do not start deep capability work while meaningful easy user-facing items remain.
rules.provenLive: PROVEN_LIVE requires the real user-facing workflow to pass. Code existing and tests passing is NOT proof.
rules.acceptanceGate: The gate is the app's own test command + tsc -b + live browser acceptance. A pre-commit hook is not the acceptance suite.
rules.costDiscipline: owned -> open-source -> self-hosted -> free tier -> partner credits -> paid. No recurring paid dependency enters quietly.
rules.honestUnavailable: A capability that is not ready must refuse truthfully rather than appear to work.

rows.anchor: FAIL answered APAC/7715.75; correct is EMEA/9930.25

runResult.attributionVerdict: DETERMINISTIC ATTRIBUTION HELD 5/5. In every row the model was forbidden to name a file and obeyed (modelNamedFile false everywhere), yet the UI still attributed the correct single file, and message fileRefs matched exactly. That is the property the fix targeted.
runResult.row3Diagnosis: NOT a grounding defect and NOT an attribution defect. Retrieval demonstrably delivered the content: asked to list the rows verbatim, the model reproduced all five INCLUDING "EMEA,Q2,9930.25,Rivera". Attribution named the right file. The model simply picked the wrong maximum with the correct data in context. REPLICATED and found PROMPT-SENSITIVE, not systematic: re-asked as "compare every revenue_eur value and state the single largest", it answered 9930.25 EMEA Q2 correctly. Separately it mis-transcribed 7715.75 as 7015.75 in the verbatim listing — a second fidelity slip by the same model.
runResult.thirdFailureMode: The rubric has buckets for (a) anchor right / attribution missing and (b) attribution present / anchor wrong => grounding defect. Row 3 is neither: grounding AND attribution both correct, the MODEL ANSWER wrong. Classification is the owner's call; not self-assigned.
runResult.contaminationNote: The first markdown run showed TWO files attributed. That was tester contamination, not product behaviour: the fixture-service.ts uploaded through the composer was still a pending attachment and rode along on that turn; fileRefs confirmed both were genuinely attached, so attribution was honest. Re-run clean afterwards and it named exactly one file.
runResult.laneStatus: NOT CLOSED. 10/10 was the stated bar and this run is 9/10.

openDefects.symptom: A vision turn held the local model for 240s and returned zero tokens; failover list contained only the failing model.
openDefects.evidence: req_775234782f08d9a87827 — brain completion_failed, consumer brain_open 240032ms, generation 0ms.
openDefects.rootCause: Same VRAM contention — a model that cannot fit retries until the deadline.

openDefects.symptom: Every grounded chat turn ends in "The engine could not complete the request" after ~240s while ComfyUI holds the GPU.
openDefects.evidence: nvidia-smi: 23723/24576 MiB used, utilization.gpu 100%, 69C, with ComfyUI /queue reporting 1 running job. Ollama /api/ps shows qwen3:8b RESIDENT at 11.5GB, so this is not a model-load failure. A direct /api/generate probe for the trivial prompt "Reply with exactly the word: READY" hung past 600s, proving the stall is in generation and is upstream of MigraPilot. Substituting the smaller qwen2.5vl:7b failed identically, so model size is not the variable.
openDefects.rootCause: Unarbitrated GPU sharing between ComfyUI (image) and Ollama (chat) on one 24GB card.
openDefects.status: OPEN — environmental, not a product defect. Chat and image generation cannot both hold the card.
openDefects.regressionTest: None yet; needs the GPU orchestration item on the backlog.
openDefects.liveAcceptance: Blocked until the card is free.
correctedClaims: CORRECTED: "two ComfyUI instances on :8188". There is ONE ComfyUI — PID 42312 (launcher), PID 23820 (worker, listening 127.0.0.1:8188), PID 41308 (comfy-tailscale-bridge.py, listening 100.86.143.93:8188). Nothing is redundant, so there is no spare instance to stop.

CORRECTED: "EASY to unblock by stopping a ComfyUI instance". ComfyUI was mid-render (/queue reported 1 running job), so stopping it would destroy in-flight owner work. The safe path is to wait for the queue to drain.

REFINED: "VRAM exhaustion" is not the whole mechanism. Generation stalls with the model already resident and with a smaller model substituted, and the card reads 100% utilisation — so compute contention matters, not just memory headroom.

openDefects.symptom: GET /api/files/index returned state "approved", searchable true, and stats files=0 chunks=0 with an EMPTY chunkCounts map. Grounded turns then told the user "No readable content was found in fixture-runbook.md" — a false statement about a file that had 4 chunks.
openDefects.evidence: Observed once at 19:50 after a brain restart. A POST reindex immediately restored 9 files / 18 chunks. NOT REPRODUCED on the next restart, where the index survived intact with all 9 counts present, so the restart itself is NOT established as the cause.
openDefects.rootCause: UNDETERMINED. Candidates: a startup race where the scoped restore has not completed while status already answers approved, or a scope-resolution miss returning zero rows silently (the pattern in scoped-mutation-row-count-invariant). Not attributed on n=1.
openDefects.status: OPEN — now REPRODUCED. Cause still not proven, but the trigger is no longer unknown.
openDefects.effort: MEDIUM — the honest-state guard is EASY; the root cause is MEDIUM.
openDefects.regressionTest: Wanted: an approved index that reports zero chunks must answer "index unavailable, reindex needed", never "no readable content was found in <file>". Approved+empty is contradictory state and must fail loudly.
openDefects.reproduction: Occurrence 2 on 2026-08-27 immediately after the brain-release activation restart. Identical signature: state "approved", searchable true, stats files=0 chunks=0, empty chunkCounts — and the live product told the user "No readable content was found in fixture-notes.txt" about a real 2-chunk file. A POST reindex restored 10 files / 23 chunks and the same question then answered correctly (MT-PLAT-7731) with attribution.
openDefects.triggerEvidence: BOTH occurrences followed a brain restart. It is NOT every restart: one intermediate restart left the index intact with all 9 counts present, so restart is a trigger but not a sufficient condition. That pattern fits a startup/lazy-restore race — status answers "approved" from the persisted record before the scoped chunk restore has populated the in-memory index — but the race has NOT been proven and must not be assumed.
openDefects.userImpact: HIGH and silent. It does not error; it states a confident falsehood about the users own file, which is worse than an outage because nothing signals that a retry would work.
openDefects.wantedFix: Approved + zero chunks is CONTRADICTORY state and must fail loudly: answer "index unavailable, reindex needed", never "no readable content was found in <file>". That guard is correct regardless of the underlying cause, so it can land before the race is proven.

openDefects.title: CSV quantitative reasoning weakness — qwen3:8b
openDefects.symptom: With all rows correctly grounded, the model can still select the wrong maximum or mistranscribe numeric values. Asked which region/quarter had the highest revenue it answered APAC/7715.75 when EMEA/9930.25 is larger, and separately transcribed 7715.75 as 7015.75.
openDefects.evidence: Layers separate cleanly and only the last one failed: correct file attached, correct chunks reached the model (it reproduced all five rows verbatim INCLUDING EMEA,Q2,9930.25), all relevant rows present, correct attribution rendered independently of model wording — then a comparison error. Rephrasing to "compare every revenue_eur value and state the single largest" produced the correct answer, so it is prompt/model-sensitive rather than retrieval loss.
openDefects.classification: NOT a Files & Documents transport, retrieval or provenance defect. A reasoning/fidelity weakness of qwen3:8b on structured tabular data. Owner ruling 2026-08-27.
openDefects.status: OPEN — separate model/tool-routing quality item; does not hold the document pipeline open.
openDefects.longerTermDirection: Do not rely on an LLM alone for arithmetic over CSV. MigraPilot should detect that a request is a DETERMINISTIC DATA OPERATION, route it through a table/data tool, and let the model explain the result rather than compute it.
openDefects.provenance: Arose from the 9/10 citation pass. That run is preserved verbatim and was NOT rewritten to 10/10.

openDefects.title: Image follow-through / conversational intent
openDefects.reportedBy: Bonex, observed in a live session 2026-08-27 (screenshots kept as acceptance evidence). NOT independently reproduced by me yet.
openDefects.symptom: With an image already active in the conversation and already successfully analysed, the follow-up "can you regenerate it?" failed to resolve against that image and asked the user to provide the content again.
openDefects.acceptanceRule: When an image is active in the conversation, follow-up references — "it", "this", "same one", "remake it", "regenerate it", "make something similar" — MUST resolve against that image unless the user clearly refers to something else.
openDefects.testMustVerify: 🚨 The resolved image actually REACHES the generation/editing routing layer. Proving the UI still displays the image is not proof; it is the same class of error as reading a rendered tile instead of the trace.
openDefects.status: OPEN — queued under high-visibility chat defects.

openDefects.title: Regeneration promise vs execution truthfulness
openDefects.symptom: MigraPilot answered "Sure! Please provide the content you'd like me to regenerate…", and then when given the image, described it again instead of regenerating or refusing honestly.
openDefects.invariant: NEVER claim an image will be regenerated unless the request is actually being routed to an available image-generation capability.
openDefects.requiredFlow: existing image + "remake/regenerate/something similar" -> recognise CREATION intent using the source image as reference -> if reference-based generation is supported, execute it and produce a new Media Library artifact WITH source provenance. If it is not supported: give a truthful capability refusal, do NOT describe the picture as though that satisfied the request, and do NOT say "Sure, I'll regenerate it".
openDefects.status: OPEN — queued under high-visibility chat defects.
openDefects.related: Same family as the image-editing refusal already shipped (IMAGE_EDITING_UNAVAILABLE): describe-instead-of-refuse is the failure mode.

pdfDocx.measuredOn: 2026-08-27, VM111, read-only probe. No code written, no packages installed.
pdfDocx.runtime: Node v22.23.2, npm 10.9.8, x86_64, Ubuntu glibc 2.39.

findings.cToolchain: ABSENT — make, g++, cc, pkg-config all missing (python3 present).
findings.existingDeps: NONE — no pdfjs-dist, pdf-parse, unpdf or mammoth in any workspace manifest.

pdfDocx.correctsAssumption: "VM111 requires pure-JS PDF extraction" was recorded as UNVERIFIED and is now REFINED rather than confirmed. The runtime does not forbid native modules; the BUILD ENVIRONMENT cannot compile them. A native module that ships prebuilt linux-x64 glibc binaries could still install. So pure-JS is the LOWEST-FRICTION path and the safe default, not a proven hard requirement.
openQuestions: Where is node_modules actually built? Releases are seeded by cp -al from the previous release, so the original install host decides whether a compiler was ever available.
Shelling out to poppler/libreoffice would mean installing system packages on VM111 — an owner decision with a dependency and attack-surface cost, not a free option.
pdfDocx.notStarted: Groundwork only. The lane does not open until the citation pass is 10/10.

deployDependencyPath.howNodeModulesArrives: cp -al HARDLINK from a prior release. Proven by inode identity: consumer node_modules/next/package.json is inode 9490805 with links=15 across 60 releases; the brain tree is inode 9453191 links=5.
deployDependencyPath.doesProductionInstall: NO install runs in the release flow. npm ci is IMPOSSIBLE in current releases because there is NO package-lock.json (older releases 867ac0f and v30 still have one; current ones do not). The historical install was "npm install --omit dev --no-audit --no-fund" run in a staging dir ON VM111 (/opt/migrapilot/staging/v6, 2026-08-16).
deployDependencyPath.nativeInstallHost: VM111 itself — x86_64, Ubuntu, glibc 2.39, identical to the runtime. So any prebuilt binary fetched there matches the runtime exactly. But VM111 has NO compiler, so only pure-JS or prebuilt-binary packages can install.
deployDependencyPath.prebuiltBinariesSurviveCpAl: YES — proven, not assumed. The consumer release carries 4 working .node binaries (@img/sharp-linux-x64, @img/sharp-linuxmusl-x64, @next/swc-linux-x64-gnu, -musl) inherited through the hardlink chain.
deployDependencyPath.doesDependencyChangeRefresh: NO — it SILENTLY INHERITS STALE. Observed in production, not induced: 5 of 12 declared consumer runtime dependencies are ABSENT from the deployed node_modules (jpeg-js, pngjs, qrcode, plus the two workspace links @migrapilot/shared-types and @migrateck/auth-client).
deployDependencyPath.whyThatIsCurrentlyHarmless: The consumer is Next.js and BUNDLES those deps into .next/server at build time — verified by finding jpeg-js, pngjs and qrcode all referenced there. Runtime node_modules is not load-bearing for bundled code.
deployDependencyPath.criticalAsymmetry: 🚨 brain-service is NOT bundled. It runs /usr/bin/node dist/src/server.js directly, so its runtime node_modules IS load-bearing. It is currently complete (13/13 declared deps present) and 100% pure JS with ZERO .node binaries. Since the indexer and exclusions.ts live in brain-service, a PDF extractor added there MUST physically exist in its runtime node_modules — and the release flow will not put it there.
deployDependencyPath.registryReachable: YES from VM111 — pdf-parse 2.4.5, unpdf 1.8.1, pdfjs-dist 6.2.108, mammoth 1.12.1 all resolve. mammoth declares no install script.

extractorClassification.pureJS: SAFE — installs without a compiler, survives the hardlink flow once installed. Preferred.
extractorClassification.prebuiltBinary: POSSIBLE and precedented (sharp), but requires an explicit install on VM111; the release flow does not deliver it.
extractorClassification.nativeCompileRequired: UNSUITABLE — no make/g++/cc on VM111 unless a build stage/toolchain is added deliberately.

deployDependencyPath.deployRisk: There is no automated deploy script for consumer/brain and no lockfile, so nothing ENFORCES a dependency install. A new brain runtime dep will be missing unless installed by hand. This should become a deploy-path fix (lockfile + explicit install step) before any load-bearing dep is added.
deployDependencyPath.keepSeparate: PDF and DOCX evaluated separately — the best extractor for each may differ.
